question: A vendor sells coffee and hot chocolate during ice hockey games. To stay in business, he must sell at least 40 coffees and 20 hot chocolates, but can not make more than 60 coffees or 35 hot chocolates. The vendor also can't make more than 75 items total. The profit on a coffee is $0.22, and the profit on a hot chocolate is $0.14. How many of each item should he sell to make the maximum profit?

candidates.code:
"""
Product-mix (production planning) model: vendor sells coffee and hot chocolate.

Decision variables
------------------
x[p]  : units of product p sold / made       p in P        NonNegativeIntegers
        (p = 'coffee', 'hot_chocolate')

Objective (MAXIMIZE)
--------------------
max  profit_coffee * x[coffee] + profit_hot_chocolate * x[hot_chocolate]

Constraints (numbered by source sentence)
-----------------------------------------
(1) x['coffee']            >= min_demand['coffee']         # "at least 40 coffees"
    x['hot_chocolate']     >= min_demand['hot_chocolate']  # "20 hot chocolates"
(2) x['coffee']            <= max_demand['coffee']         # "not more than 60 coffees"
    x['hot_chocolate']     <= max_demand['hot_chocolate']  # "35 hot chocolates"
(3) sum_p x[p]             <= total_capacity               # "not more than 75 items total"
"""

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# All numeric constants from the problem statement
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DATA = {
    "products": {                      # product -> per-product data
        "coffee": {
            "profit": 0.22,            # profit per coffee ($)
            "min_demand": 40,          # at least 40 coffees (units)
            "max_demand": 60,          # at most 60 coffees (units)
        },
        "hot_chocolate": {
            "profit": 0.14,            # profit per hot chocolate ($)
            "min_demand": 20,          # at least 20 hot chocolates (units)
            "max_demand": 35,          # at most 35 hot chocolates (units)
        },
    },
    "total_items_capacity": 75,        # at most 75 items made in total (units)
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ----- Sets -------------------------------------------------------------
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=list(d["products"].keys()))

    # Python-side data lookups (not decision variables)
    profit = {p: d["products"][p]["profit"] for p in d["products"]}
    lb = {p: d["products"][p]["min_demand"] for p in d["products"]}
    ub = {p: d["products"][p]["max_demand"] for p in d["products"]}
    capacity = d["total_items_capacity"]

    # ----- Variables --------------------------------------------------------
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.P,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=lambda m, p: (lb[p], ub[p]),
    )

    # ----- Objective --------------------------------------------------------
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(profit[p] * model.x[p] for p in model.P),
        sense=pyo.maximize,
    )

    # ----- Constraints ------------------------------------------------------
    # (1) minimum demand per product
    def min_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] >= lb[p]

    model.min_units = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=min_rule)

    # (2) maximum demand per product
    def max_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] <= ub[p]

    model.max_units = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=max_rule)

    # (3) total items cap
    def total_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= capacity

    model.total_items = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_rule)

    return model

    "min_sales": {"coffee": 40, "hot_chocolate": 20},

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "products": ["coffee", "hot_chocolate"],
    "profit": {"coffee": 0.22, "hot_chocolate": 0.14},
    "min_sell": {"coffee": 40, "hot_chocolate": 20},
    "max_sell": {"coffee": 60, "hot_chocolate": 35},
    "max_total_items": 75,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    products = d["products"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=products, ordered=True)

    # Variables: integer units sold, bounded by per-product min/max
    def sell_bounds(m, p):
        return (d["min_sell"][p], d["max_sell"][p])

    model.sell = pyo.Var(
        model.P,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=sell_bounds,
    )

    # Objective: maximise total profit
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["profit"][p] * m.sell[p] for p in m.P)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # Constraint: minimum required sales per product
    def min_sales_rule(m, p):
        return m.sell[p] >= d["min_sell"][p]

    model.min_sales = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=min_sales_rule)

    # Constraint: maximum allowed sales per product
    def max_sales_rule(m, p):
        return m.sell[p] <= d["max_sell"][p]

    model.max_sales = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=max_sales_rule)

    # Constraint: total items cannot exceed the cap
    def total_items_rule(m):
        return sum(m.sell[p] for p in m.P) <= d["max_total_items"]

    model.total_items = pyo.Constraint(rule=total_items_rule)

    return model
